details:
ÓRBITA — Plan, Simulate, Explore

ÓRBITA is an interactive educational space simulation game designed to make aerospace engineering, orbital mechanics, and Earth observation more accessible, engaging, and understandable.

How Does It Work?

In ÓRBITA, players become mission designers responsible for planning and configuring their own space missions. They select a mission objective, choose an orbital trajectory, and configure satellite components while considering engineering constraints such as mass, power consumption, communication capabilities, and mission requirements.

The game offers five orbital configurations, allowing players to explore how different orbital characteristics influence satellite performance and mission feasibility.

The project combines three main elements:

  • NASA's General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT): Used to simulate orbital trajectories and generate realistic orbital data.
  • Python and JSON: Used to process simulation results, organize satellite specifications, and integrate scientific information from NASA's SWOT and PACE missions.
  • Godot Engine: Used to create the interactive gameplay, satellite visualization, mission configuration interface, and 3D results.

The intended final experience connects the player's decisions with orbital simulation results and real Earth observation data, providing an educational assessment of the mission.

Scientific Data and NASA Resources

ÓRBITA incorporates NASA resources to connect aerospace engineering with real-world scientific applications.

The SWOT (Surface Water and Ocean Topography) mission provides scientific context related to Earth's surface water and ocean topography.

The PACE (Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, ocean Ecosystem) mission provides scientific context related to ocean ecosystems, atmospheric aerosols, and clouds.

By integrating these resources into the game's data system, ÓRBITA aims to demonstrate why satellite missions matter beyond space exploration, particularly for understanding and monitoring our planet.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes ÓRBITA different is its combination of interactive gameplay, engineering decision-making, orbital simulation, and scientific data.

Instead of simply presenting information about satellites, the game encourages players to experiment, make decisions, and understand their consequences.

Its visual approach includes a 3D satellite configuration environment, interactive mission selection, and scientific results presented in an accessible format.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ÓRBITA aims to inspire students and young developers to explore aerospace engineering, physics, programming, and Earth observation.

By transforming complex scientific concepts into interactive challenges, the project encourages curiosity, critical thinking, problem-solving, and experimentation.

Our goal is to demonstrate that learning about space does not have to be limited to textbooks or specialized laboratories. With accessible technology and real scientific resources, students can begin exploring how space missions are designed and why they matter.

Development Tools and Technical Considerations

The project uses Godot Engine for game development and 3D visualization, Python for data processing, JSON for structured data storage, and NASA GMAT for orbital simulations.

During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, performance, educational value, and the limitations of simplified space mission simulations.

We also prioritized an architecture that allows scientific datasets and orbital simulation results to be prepared in advance, reducing the need for continuous internet access or complex external integrations during gameplay.

Our Vision

ÓRBITA is more than a space simulation game. It is an educational bridge between real aerospace science and the next generation of explorers, engineers, and innovators.

We believe that understanding the universe begins with curiosity, and ÓRBITA aims to turn that curiosity into exploration.
